title.narrative: Piaui Health and Social Protection Development Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Piaui Health and Social Protection Development Project is to strengthen health surveillance, social protection, and employment service delivery systems to benefit the Borrower's vulnerable population. There are four components to the project, the first component being strengthening health surveillance systems and capacities. This component aims to strengthen the state health surveillance systems and capacities by improving their structures and introducing coordination and management mechanisms for service provision, focused on priority populations and regions of the state with weaker services. The second component is the strengthening social protection systems and capacities. This component aims to improve the state social protection and employment service delivery systems and capacities by strengthening benefits of social assistance for those in immediate need, structuring services to promote economic opportunities, and improving the state's ability to play a more effective role in overseeing and supporting the social protection and labor activities in the state, especially to respond more effectively to economic, social, and climate-related shocks. The third component is the strengthening food and nutrition surveillance and food security response. This component responds to the growing challenge, including due to climate impacts, of food insecurity in Piaui, requiring a coordinated approach. Finally, the fourth component is the project management. This component aims to strengthen the capacity of state agencies and provide overall implementation support to the Project Coordination Unit (Unidade de Coordenação do Projeto, PCU) and Project Implementation Unit (Unidades de Implementação do Projeto, PIU) in technical, environmental, social, fiduciary, supervision, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), and communications-related areas, including training and operating costs.
To strengthen health surveillance, social protection, and employment service delivery systems to benefit the state's vulnerable population.

title.narrative: PDO 4: Underweight children in priority municipalities referred to receive social assistance services and benefits

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the percentage of children under five years of age identified as underweight that are referred to receive social assistance and benefits. Monitoring weight-for-age as a basis for referrals to social assistance services can help both advance and assess the contribution of food security responses to growth promotion and reduction of child morbidity and mortality. Low weight-for-age identifies the condition of being light or underweight for a specific age and reflects the process of gaining insufficient weight relative to age or losing weight. Insufficient weight gain can have short and long term impacts on child growth and development. Identification of underweight children must trigger immediate coordinated interventions to ensure household food security toavert impacts on the child's health and wellbeing. Since weight-for-age is influenced by both the height and weight of the child, the indicator reflects both past (chronic) and/or present (acute) undernutrition. This indicator is also a measure of the health andsocial protection systems capacity to monitor and respond to health and nutritional risk in the population. Targets are set on a cumulative annual basis.

title.narrative: PDO 3: Individuals referred to job vacancies by SINE's labor intermediation service

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the number of potential employees that were matched to a vacancy and referred to it. The indicator comprehensively measures the quality of the service offered by SINE as it is determined by the state's effort to capture vacancies for the labor intermediation system, the attractiveness of the service offered by SINE to potential workers, and the ability of SINE to establish a match between workers and the vacancies offered. Progress will be assessed monthly despite targets being set on a non-cumulative annual basis.

Targets are set on a cumulative annual basis and increases are expected once territorial expansion activities begin.

title.narrative: 1.7) Trained staff who consider that the training received is useful for improving their professional performance in health and social protection services

comment.narrative: Citizen Engagement indicator. Recognizing the importance of user's satisfaction and improved capacity of professionals to deliver their services. Satisfaction surveys will be included in the end of all trainings offered. The trainings offered to the state's staff will measure their satisfaction with the training courses, namely, their perception of the usefulness of the training for the improvement of their professional performance. The survey will include an open field where the staff can provide comments and suggestions that will help inform the design of the training program for future rounds. Comments received in the open field will be analyzed and those that require a response will be answered within a maximum period of 30 days from their receipt. Targets are set non- cumulative.

title.narrative: 1.5) Municipalities that report Work-related Injuries and Diseases (DART) in the National System of Disease Notification (SINAN).

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the level of registration of work-related diseases and injuries at the municipal level. This is an important source of information for the design and implementation of the state's prevention programs and policies. Targets are set on a cumulative annual basis. Baseline is dated December 2022.

title.narrative: 1.5) Municipalities that report Work-related Injuries and Diseases (DART) in the National System of Disease Notification (SINAN).

comment.narrative: This indicator shows exceptional performance at 61% (Nov/2025), 16 percentage points above the target (45%) and 33.8 percentage points above the 2022 baseline (27.2%), indicating broad dissemination of worker health surveillance and consolidation of the reporting network.

title.narrative: 1.2) Diseases, disorders and public health events subject to mandatory reporting, notified within 24 hours and registered within seven days in the respective surveillance information system

comment.narrative: Measures the capacity to rapidly report the occurrence of those diseases, disorders and public health events that are subject to mandatory notification. Provides a measurable indicator that allows decision makers to objectively estimate the size of a health problem, and monitor the processes, results and impact of an intervention on the affected population. It provides information to implement preventive programs/policies and support the decision-making process. Targets are set on a cumulative annual basis.

title.narrative: 1.2) Diseases, disorders and public health events subject to mandatory reporting, notified within 24 hours and registered within seven days in the respective surveillance information system

comment.narrative: The indicator is above the 75% 2025 year-end target. The partial result of 82.0% represents a 32.4 percentage point increase over the 2022 baseline (49.6%), showing optimized operational workflows and a stronger alert capacity in state surveillance. The challenges are shifting from expansion to consolidation and quality improvement.

title.narrative: 1.1) Deaths among women of reproductive age investigated

comment.narrative: The partial result of 73.54% is below the 2024 target of 75% and far from the 2025 year-end target of 78%. There is potential for improvement through two structural initiatives in Piaui: the creation of 22 Investigation Centers and the approval of the Maternal and Child Care Plan, which provide institutional foundations and direction to enhance surveillance of female mortality. However, turning this potential into results is hindered by weaknesses in initial reporting, difficulty accessing complete clinical information, and bottlenecks in closing cases (waiting for reports and conclusions).

1.3) Diseases subject to mandatory and immediate notification ("Doenças de Notificação Compulsória Imediata, DNCI) classified within 60 days after notification

comment.narrative: The result of 59.9% reflects a 15.4 percentage point drop compared to the 2022 baseline (75.3%) and is well below the 80% annual targets for 2024 and 2025. Performance indicates a critical breakdown in the analysis and conclusion flow for urgent cases, with bottlenecks after notification. Main obstacles include unprioritized investigation and laboratory confirmation, team overload, and delays at reference laboratories.

title.narrative: 1.3) Diseases subject to mandatory and immediate notification ("Doenças de Notificação Compulsória Imediata, DNCI) classified within 60 days after notification

comment.narrative: Measures the ability of the state to investigate and classify those diseases that are subject to mandatory and immediate reporting (DNCI) within 60 days after being reported. The process defines whether all suspected cases are reported and included into the National System of Diseases Notification (SINAN) at the first moment of suspicion, and whether the required clinical, epidemiological, and laboratory investigations are concluded as a confirmed or discharged case in SINAN within a 60-day period after the notification. Targets are set on a cumulative annual basis.
